On 28 March 2025, tribal leaders of Sinjar district gathered in front of the Sinjar Center in Sinjar city (Ninewa) and one of the members of the Tribal Council of Sinjar read the statement of tribal shaykhs and officials, rejecting the agreement which had been reached between the federal government in Baghdad and the Kurdish government in Erbil (the Sinjar Agreement), which excluded the people of Sinjar from the agreement. The statement highlighted the history of the Yazidi community and the history of their persecutions and displacement, adding that the people of Sinjar had not been properly represented during the negotiations of the agreement. The leaders indicated that the Kurdistan Regional Government was trying to implement the agreement aimed at restoring its control over Sinjar. The statement denounced also the arrest of five members of YBS (Sinjar Resistance Units) on 18 March 2025, describing it as arbitrary and warning of possible escalation of events. The tribal leaders called on the prime minister to intervene and release the five men.

On 25 March 2025, members of the Abna Sahawat Wassit Movement protested in Kut city (Wassit) demanding appointments. They claimed they had been officially appointed three years earlier but none of them managed to start work. Nevertheless their welfare benefits had been cut for many of them and they had not been allowed to apply for other appointments since they had been registered officially as appointed. The protesters clashed with security forces and seven of them were beaten. One was in critical condition. 7 injured. There were no fatalities.

The scholars argued the men had been arrested on false charges that were not consistent with Yazidi beliefs and that the arrest was an attempt to break the will of the Yazidi people. The arrested men, according to the scholars, were heroes who had sacrificed their blood for Iraq. The scholars warned that Yazidis were being provoked by the government's actions including the arrest of the five men and that the situation may escalate. They also called on the international community and human rights associations to intervene, warning a new wave of displacements could start among the Yazidis.
